## Generated Data

The world starts with a manufacturer, here Velora AG. The manufacturer
publishes a catalog for each model year. A catalog lists cars. Each car
comes with five things: a price, a brand and model, a workshop, its parts
and a 3D model.

Velora AG was founded in 1919. Its headquarters is at
Hauptstraße 1001, Ingolstadt. Each year it publishes a new catalog: the catalog
2026 has 5 cars, the catalog 2027 has 6.

The Velora Amita is a hatchback for 18,600 EUR. The
workshop Lindqvist Motors in Wolfsburg services it.

<text x="40" y="266" class="uc-t" text-anchor="start">Every car has a bill of materials like this, 4 levels deep.</text>
<text x="40" y="288" class="uc-s" text-anchor="start">Only the first branch is opened here; the other boxes hold parts of their own.</text>

</figure>

A car is built from assemblies, like the engine and the transmission.
Each assembly contains components, each component contains parts, and the
parts are held together by screws, nuts and washers. Follow one branch:
Engine → Cylinder head → Intake valve → Hex bolt M6x20.

This list of parts is called the bill of materials. Factories, workshops
and shops all work with it.

<text x="320" y="425" class="uc-s" text-anchor="start">Shape: a piece you can see, made of a material</text>
</svg>

Every car also has a 3D model, so an app can show it on the screen. The
model is a tree: groups hold other pieces, and shapes are the pieces you
can see, each made of a material.

1 new car and 1 new price; the rest is taken over from the year before.

The same world comes in 5 sizes, from 5
cars to 20,000,000 cars. The team picks the size that fits the
test: a tiny world for a quick check, a huge one for a load test. The same
settings always give the same cars, on every computer.

<sub class="uc-note">Everything on this page is invented: brands, models, companies,
people, workshops, prices and parts. Only countries and cities are real.
Any similarity to real names is coincidental.</sub>
